messages:
Emily: Heads-up — noticed a steady uptick in 'gpu_ambient_noise_total' in eu-west1 since ~0300 UTC, and it lines up with a small cluster of Xid bursts. Putting it here so SRE + infra can eyeball dashboards and decide if we should start a card-level attribution run.
Sam: thanks. do you have a panel link? is this thermal or power noise?
Emily: panel -> https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc123/gpu-noise-attribution?orgId=1
Emily: quick summary: temp median unchanged, but we see short noisy spikes on nvlink error counters and inference_request_retries going to a single subset of cards. suspect silicon-level degradation + noisy NIC path.
Ravi: can you paste the PromQL you used? want to add to the alert rule if it's reliable.
Emily: sure: ```sum by(card_id) (increase(gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])) / sum by(card_id) (increase(gpu_kernel_jobs_total[5m])) > 0.02``` followed by ```increase(gpu_ambient_noise_total[1m]) > 3``` to isolate short bursts.
Lex: fwiw the inference path retries query we used: ```sum by(card_id) (increase(inference_request_retries_total[10m]))``` then correlated with host_network_err_count. makes it obvious when cards cause extra retries upstream.
Sam: can we augment dashboard to show top-3 correlated signals per-card (xid,ecc,nvlink,retries) — quick heatmap would be helpful. Grafana supports transform chaining for that.
Ravi: agree. also propose a transient drain threshold: if (xid_rate>0.05 AND retries_rate>5) for 10m -> mark card as candidate for warm-drain. lowers false positives.
Emily: +1. Suggest runbook snippet (dry-run first): ```infractl drain-card --card-id=$CARD --mode=warm --tag=\"xid-burst-2031-03-18\" --reason=\"correlated xid+retry spike\" --dry-run``` then remove --dry-run after 30m of observation.
Lex: cost tradeoff: warm-drain increases tail latency if pool gets tight. we should route to cross-region fallback only if region capacity utilization > 80% or if vendor fallback allowed by routing policy.
Sam: SLO thought: per-region GPU health SLO = 99.9% for 'card-availability' and 99.95% for 'inference-success-rate'. But health scoring needs to consider noisy transient spikes differently than slow decline. propose 'degradation credit' window of 1h before eviction.
Emily: prototype HealthScore formula I sketched: `HealthScore = 100 - clamp( (10*ecc_rate + 6*xid_rate + 8*nvlink_err + 12*retry_rate + 5*temp_anom), 0, 100 )`. We can tune weights after A/B.
Ravi: can we wire this into alerting as a rolling 30m average and have GrafanaBot post to this thread when a card's HealthScore < 60?
GrafanaBot: scheduled rule \"gpu-healthscore-alert\" will post if avg(healthscore_card[30m]) < 60 for any card in eu-west1. Next evaluation: 1937654400.
Lex: action items: 1) Ravi to add heatmap + top-3 correlated signals panel (eta 2d). 2) Sam to draft transient drain policy + capacity gating check (eta EOD). 3) Emily to run attribution script on the 6 flagged card-ids and post csv (eta +1h). 4) Ops-runbook update with infractl drain snippet and flake-vs-slow-decline decision flow (eta +3d).
Emily: posted csv: https://s3.internal/redwood/gpu-attrib/1937654321-euw.csv (contains card_id, xid_5m, retries_10m, nvlink_1m, healthscore). I'll update after we run a warm-drain on the top two cards.
Sam: noted. if warm-drain reduces retries but Xid persists, we should escalate to hardware replacement candidate. keep record in the card-lifecycle ticket.
Ravi: will follow up with PR to alerting rules and add the PromQL snippets to common playbooks.
Emily: thanks all, will update once warm-drain completes. :thumbsup:
